title: U.S. House · Maine's 1st District
area: Southern Maine, including Portland, Biddeford, Sanford, and the southern coastal region.

context.text: Incumbent Chellie Pingree ran unopposed in the Democratic primary (Tiffany Roberts did not make the ballot). Ronald C. Russell won the Republican primary over Joshua Pietrowicz.

summary.text: Chellie Pingree is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Maine's 1st District, serving since 2009. She previously served in the Maine Senate, including as Senate majority leader, and worked as a farmer and businesswoman in North Haven, Maine.

background.text: Born April 2, 1955, in Minneapolis, Minnesota; earned a B.A. from the College of the Atlantic in 1979.
Member of the Maine Senate from 1992 to 2000, serving as Senate majority leader from 1996 to 2000.
Worked as a farmer and businesswoman in North Haven, Maine before her political career.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture and the House Committee on Appropriations, including the Agriculture-FDA and Interior-Environment subcommittees, for the 2025-2026 Congress.
Served as Ranking Member of the Interior and Environment appropriations subcommittee in the 2023-2024 Congress.

candidates.name: Ronald C. Russell

summary.text: Ronald C. Russell is the Republican nominee for Maine's 1st Congressional District. He describes himself as a native Mainer, military veteran, and business owner.

background.text: Describes himself as a native Mainer, veteran, and business owner.

priorities.text: Calls for civility and bipartisan discourse in Congress, saying party-line legislation is often quickly reversed when power changes hands.
priorities.quote: In my view, legislation drawn strictly along party lines wastes time and money, as it is quickly discarded or reversed by executive order when the opposing party takes power.

priorities.text: Prioritizes education reform focused on core subjects (math, science, history, English) and giving parents a stronger voice in schools.

Opposes additional federal taxes on Maine residents, citing the state's already-high state and local tax burden, and supports making the tax relief from the 2025 tax law (the 'Big Beautiful Bill') permanent.
priorities.quote: We need to protect the temporary tax relief gains made by passage of the Big Beautiful Bill and make them permanent.

positions.summary: Opposes additional federal taxes on Maine residents given the state's already-high tax burden, and supports making the 2025 tax cuts permanent.
positions.quote: Maine is a high-tax state already; we face one of the highest overall state and local tax burdens in the country...we cannot afford additional Federal taxes on top of all that.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions drawn from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; no independent campaign website content reviewed.

sources.title: Ronald C. Russell - Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey
